messages:
ela: quick heads-up — i'm going to open a micro-PR to tidy the rate-limit / 429 troubleshooting page. the current doc has two conflicting JS snippets and a stale SDK anchor. i'll replace with one canonical JS snippet, a tiny curl example, and fix links. PR in ~20m.
sam: please ensure the JS snippet uses the exact hosted SDK params (maxRetries, baseMs, capMs, jitter) and shows honoring Retry-After header before backoff. lots of users copy the wrong pattern.
ops-bot: CI note: markdown-linkcheck flaked last week due to anchor renames. recommend adding an anchor-validated step to the docs CI job.
ela: will add that CI step. also adding a one-line runtime cross-ref explaining that runtime trims input to model limits before fallback selection so customers understand why fallbacks sometimes see shortened prompts.
link-bot: linkcheck: broken link detected "/docs/sdk/retry-policies-old" referenced in error-reference/429.md -> 404
sam: can you include a tiny parseRetryAfter helper that handles numeric seconds and RFC1123 http-date? parsing is a common gotcha.
ela: yes — plan is parseRetryAfter + single hosted SDK example: `await redwood.generate({ model: 'rw-small', input: prompt, retry: { maxRetries: 3, baseMs: 250, capMs: 5000, jitter: true } })` plus a concise curl snippet for ops.
devin: add one short line under "fallback behavior": "Prefer a model-variant fallback when output fidelity is critical; prefer a quantized or lower-latency fallback when cost/latency is the priority." keeps expectations clear.
ela: pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1824 — requested reviews from @sam @devin and triggered CI.
sam: quick review done, left one tiny wording nit. linkcheck is green after the anchor fix. merge when ready.
ela: merged and posted a 2-line update to #support and #runtime to reduce duplicate tickets. thanks everyone!
